Research and retry subagents (workbench/briefs/BRIEF-tax.md, BRIEF-tax-retry.md), every quote checked by the lead against its saved page.

figures.finding: A resident Yemeni national pays income tax of 0% to YER 120,000 a year, 10% to 240,000, 15% to 840,000 and 20% above; a resident foreigner pays a flat 20%; monthly salary first deducts YER 10,000 and the 7% social security contribution.
figures.applies: 2026; the text also gives salaried nationals' rates as 0% to 15%, and bonuses, fees and commissions at a flat 15%.

sources.said: Up to 120,000 0% Over 120,000 and up to 240,000 10% Over 240,000 and up to 840,000 15% Over 840,000 20% Individual income tax rate: Resident foreigners 20%
Salary paid as overtime or leave pay, commissions, fees, bonuses, gratuities, and benefits are taxable at the flat rate of 15%.
Deductions and allowances available on monthly salary income include YER 10,000 (monthly exemption limit); 7% of gross salary for an employee’s social security contribution

figures.finding: Under the Sana'a government the employer pays 13% and the employee 7% of salary to the General Corporation for Social Security.
figures.applies: 2026; areas outside Sana'a's administration not described.

sources.said: Employers operating under the Sana’a government must contribute 13% of a national or foreign employee's salary to the General Corporation for Social Security (GCSS); the employee contributes 7%.

figures.finding: The employer calculates and deducts payroll tax and files the return within the first 10 days of the following month; individuals generally file no return.

sources.said: The employer is responsible for calculating and deducting payroll tax from its employees’ salaries and for remitting it to the government on behalf of the employee.
The tax return must be submitted to the tax authority within the first 10 days of the following month.

figures.finding: A non-resident pays a flat 20% on income earned from Yemen; copyright royalties paid to a non-resident bear 10% withholding.

sources.said: A flat rate of 20% applies to resident foreign employees and a flat rate of 20% applies to nonresidents.
A 10% withholding tax applies to payments made to a nonresident in respect of commissions, patents, trademarks, and copyright royalties

figures.finding: Yemen levies a general sales tax of 5% (10% on some telecommunications); registration is required above YER 50 million of annual turnover.

sources.said: The general rate is 5%, although a 10% rate applies to some telecommunications and mobile communications products or services.
Companies whose annual turnover exceeds YER 50 million or its equivalent are required to register for sales tax purposes.

figures.finding: The tax year is the calendar year; employees' tax is settled monthly by the employer.

sources.said: Tax year: The tax year is the calendar year. Filing status:
